findings.conditions: sc_notify_payloadv with type NBX and sorted=0, any rank with a nonempty receiver list
findings.reasoning: sc_notify_payloadv_nbx posts its MPI_Issend with tag SC_TAG_NOTIFY_NBXV (line 2058), but the MPI_Iprobe(ANY_SOURCE) at 2087 and the MPI_Recv at 2106 use SC_TAG_NOTIFY_NBX, a different enum value. Nobody ever receives the NBXV messages, the synchronous sends never complete, Testall never succeeds, so no rank calls Ibarrier and every rank loops forever. The tests only run payloadv with sorted=1, which goes through the wrapper, so this path is untested. The probe can also take an NBX message that a faster rank sent in a following sc_notify_payload_nbx call. That records a wrong sender, sizes the data from the wrong message and corrupts the offsets.

findings.conditions: two consecutive SUPERSET notify calls on one communicator; one rank finishes call 1 early while another is still in its probe loop
findings.reasoning: The superset loop counts num_super_senders messages taken with Iprobe(ANY_SOURCE) on SUPER_TRUE or SUPER_EXTRA. Nothing synchronizes at the end of a call, and the TRUE sends of the next call are posted before compute_superset. A rank A that finished call 1 can therefore Isend a call-2 TRUE message to B while B is still waiting for some rank C in call 1. Per-source ordering does not stop this: A's call-1 message may have been an EXTRA, which has a different tag. B then counts A's call-2 message, records A as a true sender with call-2 payload, and stops early. C's call-1 message leaks into call 2. The result is wrong senders and payloads, a failed bsearch assertion, or a count mismatch that makes a later call hang.

findings.conditions: back-to-back NBX notify calls on the same communicator; one rank sees the Ibarrier complete before another rank's next Test
findings.reasoning: The NBX loop runs Iprobe(ANY_SOURCE, SC_TAG_NOTIFY_NBX) before MPI_Test on the barrier request. Once the Ibarrier completes globally, a fast rank A leaves, enters the next sc_notify_payload_nbx call and Issends to B with the same tag and communicator. B can run Iprobe once more before its Test reports done and take A's next-round message in the current call. B then reports a spurious sender with the wrong payload in call 1 and misses A in call 2. If the payload sizes of the two calls differ, the MPI_Recv at 1979 is truncated and aborts. The same pattern exists in payloadv_nbx at line 2087.

findings.conditions: NARY notify called repeatedly; mpisize not a full tree so wrapped senders exist; one rank is slow at a level
findings.reasoning: Every one of the nrecv receives at a level is an MPI_Probe(ANY_SOURCE, tag), and the tag depends only on the level, not on the call. A rank S in a short group sends to B through the wrapped peer without depending on B's progress. S can finish call 1 and send B its call-2 message with the same tag while B still waits for another source C. B's probe then matches S a second time and computes the same slot j. That slot is re-initialized (leaking the first buffer), and C's slot in recvbufs is never initialized, so sc_notify_merge reads garbage. C's message is consumed in the next call.
